rows.title: Freedom Flex Q4: grocery stores, dining & American Red Cross donations
rows.description: Q4 2026 5% categories (Oct 1 – Dec 31): grocery stores (Walmart and Target excluded), dining/restaurants, and American Red Cross donations. Activation deadline is Dec 14, 2026 — Chase's structure is retroactive to Oct 1 as long as you activate by that date, so there's no rush, but don't forget it. Some outlets report Freedom Flex's card-level dining bonus stacks for ~7% total on dining this quarter for Flex cardholders specifically — worth confirming the exact stack math against Chase's own terms before relying on it.
rows.earn_cap_note: 5% on up to $1,500 combined per quarter after activation, then 1%. Retroactive to Oct 1 as long as you activate by Dec 14.
rows.verdict: Grocery + dining is one of the most broadly usable Freedom Flex quarters of the year — plenty of runway to activate since it's retroactive through Dec 14, but do it now so you don't forget.
rows.end_label: Quarter runs Oct 1 – Dec 31; activate by Dec 14
rows.source_label: Chase (Q4 announcement) + Doctor of Credit + NerdWallet + AwardWallet + Upgraded Points

rows.title: Citi Dividend Q4: Citi Travel bookings + restaurants
rows.description: Q4 2026 5% categories (starting Oct 1): Citi Travel bookings (hotels, car rentals, attractions booked through the Citi Travel portal — airfare excluded) and restaurants (cafes, bars, lounges, fast food). Enrollment required each quarter — not automatic, and not retroactive; earning starts within ~2 business days of enrolling. Note: Citi Dividend is reportedly no longer open to new applicants — this is for existing cardholders.
rows.earn_cap_note: $300 ANNUAL cash-back cap across all quarters combined (≈$6,000/yr spend at 5%) — not a per-quarter cap. Enroll before spending; Citi doesn't backdate.
rows.verdict: Enroll now if you have a Citi Travel booking or restaurant spend coming up — Citi's $300/year cap means it's worth checking how much of it you've already used this year before leaning on Q4.
rows.end_label: Quarter runs Oct 1 – Dec 31; enroll first
rows.source_label: Doctor of Credit + Upgraded Points + Forbes Advisor

rows.title: US Bank Cash+: Q4 category selection — window unclear, check your account today
rows.description: Still no clean answer on whether Q4 selection can still be made (AwardWallet: selection opens 45 days before the quarter and runs until 5 days before the end of the current quarter, no exact dates). Not in dispute: selections are NEVER retroactive — 5%/2% starts ~3 business days after you select, so earnings already missed in early October stay missed. If you have not picked, check your account today at usbank.com; if the option is still offered, choose 2 categories now. 12-category roster unchanged.
rows.earn_cap_note: 5% on first $2,000/quarter combined across your 2 chosen categories, then 1%. No selection = no 5% at all that quarter. Pick a few days before Sep 26 so Oct 1 starts earning.
rows.verdict: Selections are never retroactive — if the option is still in your account, pick today so the rest of the quarter counts.
rows.end_label: Window unclear — check your account today
rows.source_label: US Bank (KB0069468) + AwardWallet

rows.title: Discover it Q4: restaurants, entertainment, utilities — activation open now
rows.description: Q4 2026 5% categories, announced Sep 1: Restaurants, Entertainment (movies, concerts, live sports — first time this category has appeared), and Utilities (recurring household bills like electricity, water, internet, phone). Quarter runs Oct 1 – Dec 31. 5% starts only AFTER activation — Discover is never retroactive, so activate now.
rows.earn_cap_note: 5% on up to $1,500 per quarter (max $75 back), then 1%. NOT retroactive — earning starts at activation, so activate before Oct 1. Activation opened Sep 1.
rows.verdict: Restaurants + utilities is one of the most universally usable quarters Discover has run — nearly everyone has both. Activate today; every unactivated day after Oct 1 is 5% left on the table.
rows.source_label: Discover + Doctor of Credit + Upgraded Points + NerdWallet

rows.title: Points Boost / The Edit: 2.5¢ tier is gone — most hotels now 1.65¢
rows.description: The 11-property 2.5¢/pt tier (Apr–Jul) is dead — the '2.5X Points Boost' articles still circulating are that expired batch. Most Edit hotels sit at 1.65¢ (~41% still at 2.0¢); floor is 1.15¢; rates rotate silently per property in both directions (Chase changed the terms from 'guaranteed 2x' to 'up to 2x' in Dec 2025). Flights: up to 1.75¢ domestic premium (Alaska/JetBlue/Southwest only), 2.0¢ international.
rows.verdict: Never assume the rate — check your exact property and dates in Chase Travel before positioning points; 1.65¢ is the realistic ceiling for most bookings.
rows.source_label: Chase (official guide) + Frequent Miler + Upgraded Points

rows.title: Home Depot card: up to $100 off first purchase — through Jan 2027
rows.description: First-purchase discount: $25 off $25–$299, $50 off $300–$999, $100 off $1,000+, valid through Jan 27, 2027. Discount must be used within 30 days of account opening; single transaction; excludes gift cards, installation, tool rental, select premium brands. Standing 6-month deferred-interest financing on $299+ continues. Note: the end date for the longer (12–24mo) promotional financing on installed windows/HVAC/water treatment/blinds/custom closets is unconfirmed — check with Home Depot before relying on it.
rows.verdict: Only worth a new account if a $1,000+ project purchase is imminent — and deferred-interest financing bites at ~30% retroactive if not paid in full.
rows.source_label: Home Depot credit center + WalletHub + NerdWallet

rows.title: Best Buy Visa: certificate ratio holds at 250 pts = $5 (2.0¢/pt)
rows.description: Certificate ratio: 250 My Best Buy points = $5 certificate (2.0¢/pt); no devaluation found. New cardholders: 10% back (double the standard 5%) on purchases made in the first 14 days after account opening. Standing rates otherwise unchanged: 5% at Best Buy, 3% gas, 2% grocery/dining, 1% elsewhere; no annual fee (Platinum variant — the separate Gold variant carries a $59 AF). Don't confuse this card's ratio with Best Buy's separate My Best Buy Plus/Total membership 'reward points' program launched in 2026 — different program, doesn't affect this card's certificate math.
rows.verdict: Still a clean 2.0¢ certificate ratio with nothing to act on — except new cardholders, who should front-load big purchases into their first 14 days to catch the 10% rate.
rows.source_label: Best Buy + WalletHub + US News

rows.title: CSR DoorDash: restaurant credit jumping to $15/month (up to $35/mo total) — effective Oct 1
rows.description: CHANGED: as part of Sapphire Reserve's 10th-anniversary refresh, Chase is raising the existing $5/month DoorDash restaurant credit to $15/month (usable on ANY DoorDash order, not just restaurants) effective Oct 1, 2026 — stacking with the existing two $10/month non-restaurant (grocery/retail) credits for up to $35/month in DoorDash-linked value (each still needs a $20 minimum order per DoorDash's terms). Free DashPass membership continues; the enrollment deadline to lock in complimentary DashPass was extended to Dec 31, 2027. The overall benefit runs through Dec 31, 2029.
rows.verdict: A real, dated improvement — from Oct 1 this is worth up to $420/year if you use it fully, triple the old restaurant-credit value. Re-check your DashPass enrollment status before Dec 31, 2027 either way.
rows.end_label: Credit increase effective Oct 1, 2026; benefit runs through Dec 31, 2029
rows.source_label: Chase (10th-anniversary announcement) + Thrifty Traveler + Doctor of Credit + One Mile at a Time

rows.title: Amex Platinum: re-enroll for Hertz President's Circle by Dec 31
rows.description: Amex's Hertz Gold Plus Rewards President's Circle benefit requires re-enrollment through the new Amex flow by Dec 31, 2026 — otherwise the status (and Amex CDP discount code) may drop off your Hertz profile. Applies to Platinum, Business Platinum, Morgan Stanley/Schwab Platinum, Delta Reserve + Reserve Business. Re-enroll via amex.com Benefits → Car Rental Privileges (72-hr processing). No extension has been announced.
rows.verdict: Two minutes of clicking to keep free top-tier rental status — do it before the December scramble.
rows.source_label: Frequent Miler + Upgraded Points + Your Mileage May Vary

rows.title: United × Lyft: 1,000 miles for linking + 2 rides (new Lyft users)
rows.description: Link your MileagePlus account as your active Lyft partner and take 2 eligible rides within 30 days (US/PR) to earn 1,000 bonus miles — new Lyft users only. Ongoing since Nov 2025, still listed active. Standing Lyft earn rates with United linked: 4x scheduled airport rides, 3x premium + on-demand airport, 1x standard. Reminder: Lyft allows only ONE active earning partner at a time (Atmos is the other major option, at 2x/3x, stacking to 4x/6x with free Lyft Business Rewards enrollment; Bilt and Hilton are also single-partner alternatives).
rows.verdict: Free 1,000 miles if you're new to Lyft anyway — but pick your ONE Lyft partner deliberately based on how you actually fly and ride.
rows.source_label: Frequent Miler

rows.title: Amex Offer: select Hyatt properties — $100 back on $500+
rows.description: Widely reported — targeted, check your account. Pay at the hotel (no prepaid rates); select Hyatt Regency, Grand Hyatt, Centric, Destination properties in US/Mexico/Central America/Caribbean.
rows.verdict: Add it now even without a trip planned — it sits on the card until November.
rows.source_label: LoyaltyLobby + Frequent Miler (widely reported — targeted)

rows.title: Amex Offer: Hilton luxury brands — $250 back on $1,250+
rows.description: Widely reported — targeted, check your account. Waldorf Astoria, Conrad, LXR in US + Latin America (incl. Mexico, Anguilla, French Polynesia). Through Nov 30. This is a recurring/evolving offer family — smaller historical variants ($180/$750, $200/$1,000) have run in parallel on other accounts.
rows.verdict: 20% back on stays that expensive is meaningful — narrower audience, but check if you hold a premium Amex.
rows.source_label: Frequent Miler + Doctor of Credit (widely reported — targeted)

rows.title: Amex Offer: Small Luxury Hotels — $100 back on $300+
rows.description: Widely reported (Sep 1) — targeted, check your account. Spend $300+ on room rate and room charges at participating Small Luxury Hotels of the World properties and get $100 back, through Nov 15. THE CATCH: book direct at slh.com and PAY AT THE HOTEL at check-out — prepaid reservations (online or phone) are excluded, as are gift cards and amenities.
rows.verdict: 33% back on a luxury independent stay you'd book anyway is one of the richer hotel Amex Offers running — but the pay-at-hotel requirement is easy to trip on; choose a non-prepaid rate or the credit never triggers.
rows.source_label: Doctor of Credit + Frequent Miler + Upgraded Points (widely reported — targeted)

rows.title: Chase Offer: $100 back on $600+ at Chase Travel
rows.description: Widely reported — targeted, check your account. The original Jul 1–Sep 30 wave has ended; a second wave (Sep 16–Dec 14, 2026) is live for Sapphire, Freedom, Ink and J.P. Morgan Reserve cardholders — the same $100 back on a single $600+ Chase Travel booking. Check your own Offers tab for the exact end date on your account.
rows.verdict: If a portal booking is coming up anyway, this is a free ~17% back — check the Offers tab before booking and note your own expiration date.
rows.source_label: Doctor of Credit + Upgraded Points + Frequent Miler (widely reported — targeted)

rows.title: Delta Amex cards: 2,000 miles per $2,000 spent, up to 3x
rows.description: Widely reported — targeted, check your account. Enrollment-based spend promo on Delta co-brands: 2,000 bonus miles per $2,000 spent, up to 3 times (6,000 miles max), within 90 days of enrollment. Enrollment-based with no fixed end date — treat as check-your-account.
rows.verdict: Effectively +1 mile per dollar on spend you'd put somewhere anyway — enroll if it shows, but don't manufacture spend for it.
rows.source_label: AwardWallet + Upgraded Points (widely reported — targeted)

rows.title: Hilton Surpass: 13,500 bonus points per $4,500 spent, up to 3x
rows.description: Widely reported — targeted, check your account. Amex Offer on the Hilton Surpass: spend $4,500 and get 13,500 bonus Honors points, repeatable up to three times (40,500 points on $13,500). Add the offer to your card before spending; no end date published. Broader Hilton-family targeted spend-tier offers are also circulating this month on other Hilton Amex cards (reported tiers like $1,000→5,000 bonus points and $2,000→9,000, plus a supermarket-specific 3x variant) — check your specific card's Offers tab, as terms and caps vary by account and card.
rows.verdict: 40,500 Hilton points ≈ $200 of hotel value on $13,500 of spend you'd have to do anyway — a solid ~1.5% kicker, not a reason to shift real spend to a Hilton card. Enroll if it shows.
rows.source_label: Doctor of Credit + Frequent Miler (widely reported — targeted)

rows.title: Sapphire Preferred: 75,000 points
rows.description: Guaranteed 75,000 bonus points after $5,000 in purchases in the first 3 months — single tranche, no conditional mechanics. Annual fee $95, not waived. No public deadline. Targeted offers may run higher — check before applying.
rows.verdict: The everyday level — the 100K all-time high ran earlier in 2026 and is gone, so nothing about this window compels action; history says elevated offers return.
rows.source_label: Chase (product page) + uscreditcardguide.com

rows.title: Sapphire Reserve: 100,000 points
rows.description: Guaranteed 100,000 bonus points after $6,000 in purchases in the first 3 months — single tranche. Annual fee $795 ($195 per authorized user), not waived. No public deadline. The card ran a record 150K window Apr 30–Jun 15, 2026 and stepped back to 100K after that. Targeted offers may run higher — check before applying.
rows.verdict: The everyday level — a step down from the card's 2026 peak (150K), but the card's original 2016 debut level. At a $795 fee, the bonus alone shouldn't drive the decision; the credits math has to work for you.
rows.source_label: Chase (product page) + uscreditcardguide.com

rows.title: Amex Gold: as high as 100,000 points — apply-to-reveal
rows.description: Up to 100,000 Membership Rewards points after $8,000 in eligible purchases in the first 6 months. ENTIRELY conditional: Amex reveals your personalized number only after you apply; there is no guaranteed tranche. Annual fee $325, not waived. No public deadline. Note: the spend requirement rose from $6,000 to $8,000 in April 2026, so the 100K ceiling is technically unchanged but harder to hit than it used to be. Targeted offers may run higher — check before applying.
rows.verdict: 100K is the ceiling, not a promise — and the spend hurdle got 33% tougher this year, so the honest framing is 'same peak number, harder to hit,' not a newly elevated offer.
rows.source_label: Amex (product page; number via Upgraded Points + The Points Guy — rendered at application)

rows.title: Amex Platinum: as high as 175,000 points — apply-to-reveal
rows.description: Up to 175,000 Membership Rewards points after $12,000 in eligible purchases in the first 6 months. ENTIRELY conditional: personalized apply-to-reveal structure — 175K is the ceiling, many applicants see less. The spend requirement rose from $8,000 to $12,000 in Feb 2026. Annual fee $895, not waived. No public deadline. Targeted offers may run higher — check before applying.
rows.verdict: The 175K ceiling has been the running headline since mid-2025 — not a special window, and the real gate (a 50% higher spend requirement than a year ago) makes it tougher than the headline suggests.
rows.source_label: Amex (product page; number via The Points Guy + Upgraded Points)

rows.title: Citi Strata Premier: 60,000 points
rows.description: Guaranteed 60,000 ThankYou points after $4,000 in purchases in the first 3 months — single tranche. Annual fee $95, not waived. 48-month rule applies for bonus eligibility. No public deadline. Targeted offers may run higher — check before applying.
rows.verdict: This is the LOW end of the card's historical range — 75K and 80K have both run before. Unless you need ThankYou points now, waiting for the next elevated window is the sharper play.
rows.source_label: Citi (product page)

rows.title: Capital One Venture: 75,000 miles + $300 stays credit — limited-time, raised Sep 8
rows.description: RAISED Sep 8, 2026 (limited time, no published deadline): guaranteed 75,000 bonus miles after $4,000 in purchases within the first 3 months, PLUS a $300 stays credit for hotel and vacation-rental bookings through Capital One Travel — usable as a lump sum or across multiple bookings, expires at the end of the first cardholder year. Annual fee $95, not waived. Venture X is NOT included in this promotion. Targeted offers may run higher — check before applying.
rows.verdict: A real elevation — the long-running 75K standard just gained $300 of genuine (if portal-locked) value, pushing first-year value past $1,000. If a Venture was on your list, this is the best public window since the 100K days; 'limited time' with no date means don't dawdle.
rows.source_label: Capital One (via The Points Guy + Upgraded Points + Roame)

rows.title: Capital One Venture X: 75,000 miles
rows.description: Guaranteed 75,000 bonus miles after $4,000 in purchases within the first 3 months — single tranche. Annual fee $395, not waived (offset by $300 travel credit + 10K anniversary miles). No public deadline. The sibling Venture (non-X) got a limited-time $300 stays credit added Sep 8; Venture X did NOT (the $300 annual travel credit that surfaces in Venture X search results is a separate, standing card benefit, not a welcome-offer add-on). Targeted offers may run higher — check before applying.
rows.verdict: Everyday level — a 100K window ran in Nov 2025 and history suggests holiday-season elevations; if you can wait until Q4, watch for it. Oddly, the cheaper Venture currently carries the richer offer.
rows.source_label: Capital One (product page)

rows.title: Bilt Palladium: 50,000 points + $300 Bilt Cash + Gold status
rows.description: Bilt 2.0's premium card (Cardless-issued): $300 Bilt Cash posts at account opening (guaranteed) + 50,000 Bilt Points after $4,000 Everyday Spend within 90 days (conditional) + Bilt Gold elite status. Annual fee $495 ($95/AU), not waived. Sibling cards: Obsidian ($95 AF) gets $200 Bilt Cash, Blue ($0 AF) gets $100 Bilt Cash — neither has a points bonus. No public deadline. Targeted offers may run higher — check before applying.
rows.verdict: The only Bilt card with a points bonus — but $495 is steep unless the rent-earning math already works for you; the offer shouldn't be the reason.
rows.source_label: Bilt (offer-terms page)

rows.title: Autograph Journey: 60,000 points
rows.description: Guaranteed 60,000 bonus points after $4,000 in purchases in the first 3 months ($600 toward travel) — single tranche. Annual fee $95, not waived. No public deadline. Note: a 100K version exists but is restricted to Wells Fargo Premier clients (targeted — excluded from headline). Targeted offers may run higher — check before applying.
rows.verdict: Unchanged since the card's 2024 launch — the everyday level. The draw is the transfer-partner access (both Autograph cards transfer), not the bonus size.
rows.source_label: Wells Fargo (via AwardWallet + ChurnCards)

rows.title: World of Hyatt Card: up to 60,000 points (30K guaranteed)
rows.description: Current public offer: guaranteed 30,000 points after $3,000 spend in the first 3 months, plus up to 30,000 more via 2 bonus points per $1 (doubled points on top of base earn) on up to $15,000 spent in the first 6 months — the full 60K costs $15,000 of total spend. Annual fee $95, not waived. The guaranteed tranche fell from 45K to 30K on Aug 20. Targeted offers may run higher — check before applying.
rows.verdict: A below-average level — the guaranteed tranche fell from 45K to 30K on Aug 20. Don't chase this one; Hyatt card offers cycle, and 60–75K windows recur.
rows.source_label: Chase (product page)

rows.title: Delta SkyMiles Gold: as high as 80,000 miles + $250 credit — ends Nov 4
rows.description: Raised Aug 27 (Amex's best-ever Delta batch): as high as 80,000 bonus miles PLUS a $250 statement credit after $3,000 in eligible purchases in the first 6 months. Still Amex's variable structure — 80K is the ceiling, no guaranteed miles tranche. Annual fee $0 intro first year, then $150. Public deadline Nov 4, 2026. Sibling offers: Platinum up to 90K + $300/$4,000; Reserve two round-trip Comfort+ certificates + 50K/$10,000. Targeted offers may run higher — check before applying.
rows.verdict: Historically strong window — the $250 credit on top of the 80K ceiling is new, and the $0 first-year fee makes peeking at your real number cheap. If a Delta card was on your list, the Nov 4 deadline is a legitimate forcing function.
rows.source_label: Amex (product page; structure via uscreditcardguide.com + The Points Guy — rendered at application)

rows.title: Southwest Priority: 60,000 points (Plus 50K / Premier 55K)
rows.description: Guaranteed 60,000 points after $2,000 in purchases in the first 3 months on the Priority ($229 AF). Sibling consumer tiers: Plus 50K/$1,000 ($99 AF), Premier 55K/$1,500 ($149 AF). Fees not waived; no public deadline; no Companion Pass promo currently attached to the consumer cards. Targeted offers may run higher — check before applying.
rows.verdict: Standard levels across all three consumer tiers — the play is timing a Southwest card for a Companion Pass year.
rows.source_label: Chase (Southwest hub)

rows.title: United Explorer: up to 60,000 miles (50K guaranteed)
rows.description: Guaranteed 50,000 miles after $3,000 in purchases in the first 3 months, plus 10,000 more for adding an authorized user in the first 3 months. Annual fee $0 intro first year, then $150. 24-month rule applies. No public deadline. Targeted offers may run higher — check before applying.
rows.verdict: Everyday level — elevated Explorer promos have hit 70–100K historically, so this isn't a window worth rushing unless you need the miles now.
rows.source_label: Chase (product page) + Doctor of Credit

rows.title: Marriott Boundless: 3 Free Night Awards (up to 150K pts of value)
rows.description: Guaranteed 3 Free Night Awards (each worth up to 50,000 points/night — up to 150K points of value; delivered as certificates not points) after $3,000 in purchases in the first 3 months, plus up to $100 in airline statement credits ($50 semi-annually after $250 airline spend per period; usable through Jun 30, 2027). Annual fee $95, not waived. No stated deadline. The earlier elevated 4-Free-Night window is gone. Targeted offers may run higher — check before applying.
rows.verdict: Standard-good, not peak — some past promos hit 4–5 Free Night Awards; 3 is the card's normal running level. Used well against the right property, still beats a typical points bonus.
rows.source_label: Chase (product page) + Doctor of Credit

rows.title: IHG One Rewards Premier: 180,000 points
rows.description: Guaranteed 180,000 points after $3,000 in purchases in the first 3 months, plus 10,000 more for adding an authorized user in the first 3 months (up to 190K total). Annual fee $150, not waived. Offer runs through Nov 18. Targeted offers may run higher — check before applying.
rows.verdict: Strong for this card — the highest public level in this feed (up to 175K before). At IHG's ~0.5¢ values, 180K ≈ $900 of hotel value; worth applying now if you want the card.
rows.source_label: Chase (product page)

rows.title: Hilton Surpass: 130,000 points + Free Night Reward (fee waiver still gone)
rows.description: 130,000 Honors points PLUS a Free Night Reward after $3,000 in eligible purchases in the first 6 months — public deadline Jan 13, 2027. The Free Night Reward is valid for 12 months from issuance. The $150 annual fee applies from year one (waiver removed Sep 10, not restored). Amex refreshed the broader Hilton Amex family again on Sep 18, 2026 (Aspire boosted to up to a reported 200K, entry-level Hilton Honors card gained a Free Night Reward) — Surpass's own terms here are unaffected by that refresh. Targeted offers may run higher — check before applying.
rows.verdict: Net RICHER than the outgoing 130K + fee-waiver version for most people: a Free Night Reward is worth $400+ used well, comfortably beating the $150 first-year fee you now pay. Multiple outlets call this the best Surpass sign-up bonus on record.
rows.source_label: Amex (offer via nyreport.com + NerdWallet + The Points Guy — rendered at application)

rows.title: Citi AAdvantage Platinum Select: 80,000 miles
rows.description: Guaranteed 80,000 AAdvantage miles after $3,500 in purchases in the first 4 months. Annual fee $0 intro first year, then $99. The page warns the offer is session-based ('may not be available if you leave this page') — no published end date. Context: Citi is becoming AA's exclusive US co-brand issuer (Barclays Aviator portfolio acquired). Targeted offers may run higher — check before applying.
rows.verdict: Elevated — 50K is the baseline, so 80K with a first-year fee waiver is one of the stronger co-brand offers running. Session-based availability means grab it in one sitting if you want it.
rows.source_label: AA/Citi (official direct page)

rows.title: Atmos Ascent (ex-Alaska Visa): LOWERED to 50,000 points + $99 Companion Fare
rows.description: The current public headline, verified on Bank of America's own product page and cross-checked against The Points Guy's current-offers page, is 50,000 bonus points + $99 Companion Fare (plus taxes/fees from $23) after $1,500 in purchases in the first 90 days — down from the 70,000 pts / $2,500 spend offer that ran into September. Annual fee $95, not waived. Several stale articles still cite 70K/$2,500, and one shows an expired 85,000-pt version. Targeted offers may run higher — check before applying.
rows.verdict: A real drop from the earlier 70K — the lowest public level we've tracked for this card. The annual Companion Fare remains the long-term value driver regardless of the sign-up number.
rows.source_label: Bank of America (via uscreditcardguide.com + AwardWallet)

rows.title: American AAdvantage points sale: up to 40% discount (2.26¢/mile)
rows.description: American is selling AAdvantage miles at up to 40% off — about 2.26¢ per mile at the best tier. No end date stated.
rows.verdict: Skip: 2.26¢ is above typical AAdvantage value (~1.5–1.7¢). Top-off only, never speculative.
rows.source_label: Upgraded Points

rows.title: Marriott Bonvoy points sale: 55% bonus (0.81¢/pt)
rows.description: Marriott is selling Bonvoy points with a 55% bonus — about 0.81¢ per point — through Nov 23, max 200,000 points per transaction.
rows.verdict: Skeptical: Bonvoy points are worth roughly 0.7–0.9¢, so 0.81¢ is break-even. Top-off only; if you hold Ultimate Rewards, Chase's 70% Marriott transfer bonus (through Oct 15) is cheaper.
rows.source_label: Upgraded Points

rows.title: Chase co-brand cards: Q4 cardmember spend promos (Oct 1–Dec 31)
rows.description: Widely reported — targeted, check your account. Chase emailed Q4 "My Chase Bonus" spend offers on Sep 29 for co-brand cardholders (most often seen: United, Aeroplan, IHG, Marriott, Hyatt, Prime Visa). Reported structures: 5X/7X/9X/10X on up to $1,000 at grocery/gas/restaurants, or flat bonuses (e.g. 3,000 points after $3,000, 6,000 after $6,000, 5,000 after $9,000). Terms vary by account and card; no single register-by date is published (one unverified snippet cites Oct 14 for a Marriott offer). Running Oct 1–Dec 31; register at chase.com/mybonus.
rows.verdict: Free points on spending you were doing anyway — register on any offer you see, then forget it.
rows.source_label: Doctor of Credit + Travel-on-Points + Upgraded Points (widely reported — targeted)

rows.title: Amex Offer: $50 back on $200 at Frontier Airlines
rows.description: Widely reported — targeted, check your account. Amex Offer: $50 statement credit on a $200+ Frontier purchase, spend by Dec 31, 2026. Add the offer to your card first.
rows.verdict: 25% back on a flight you were buying anyway — Frontier fares are cheap, so confirm the total beats other carriers.
rows.source_label: InsideFlyer (widely reported — targeted)

rows.title: Amex Offer: $40 on $200 or $60 on $400 at JetBlue (booked direct)
rows.description: Widely reported — targeted, check your account. Amex Offer for JetBlue bookings made on jetblue.com — $40 back on $200 or $60 back on $400 depending on your offer — expires Dec 14, 2026.
rows.verdict: Up to 15–20% back on JetBlue fares — worth adding if you fly JetBlue anyway.
rows.source_label: InsideFlyer (widely reported — targeted)

rows.title: Hilton Aspire: 200,000 points + free night reward
rows.description: 200,000 Hilton Honors points after $6,000 in eligible purchases in the first 6 months, plus the annual Free Night Reward; public window Sep 10, 2026 – Jan 13, 2027. Confirm the annual fee on the application page. Targeted offers may run higher — check before applying.
rows.verdict: Reported as a record Aspire public offer — a historically strong window, though the $6,000 spend is the highest of the Hilton family.
rows.source_label: The Points Guy + Traveling for Miles

rows.title: Hilton Honors points sale: 120% bonus (0.45¢/pt)
rows.description: Hilton is selling Honors points with a 120% bonus on purchases of 5,000+ points — about 0.45¢ per point — through Nov 21, max 240,000 points per calendar year. May be targeted: the bonus you see when signed in could be smaller.
rows.verdict: Hilton points are worth roughly 0.4–0.5¢, so 0.45¢ is about break-even: top off a specific booked stay only, and check the price on Hilton's site before buying.
